title: Creating a Sahla Pay account
text:
Creating a Sahla Pay account
Section: Account > Getting started
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Opening an account takes a few minutes in the app. You'll need a phone number from the country you live in, and your ID if you want to verify straight away.

## Before you start

- Check you're eligible. See Who can open a Sahla Pay account.
- Use a phone number registered in your name. It becomes your login and receives your security codes.
- Have your ID with you. You can skip verification for now, but your limits will be lower.

## Create your account

To sign up:

1. Download the Sahla Pay app from the App Store or Google Play.
2. Tap **Create account** and enter your mobile number.
3. Enter the code we send by SMS.
4. Add your full name exactly as it appears on your ID, your date of birth and your email.
5. Create a password and, if your phone supports it, turn on fingerprint or face login.
6. Tap **Verify now** to scan your ID and take a selfie, or **Later** to skip.

## What happens next

Your account is ready to receive money and top up as soon as you finish step 5. Until you verify, it works with the limits for unverified accounts; see Unverified vs verified accounts. When you're ready to add money, see Getting started: your first top-up.

title: Who can open a Sahla Pay account
text:
Who can open a Sahla Pay account
Section: Account > Eligibility
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Sahla Pay accounts are personal accounts for individuals who live in Saudi Arabia, the UAE or Egypt. You open your account in the country where you hold a valid ID, and the app sets your country from the phone number you register with. You can't change it later without opening a new account (see Moving to another country).

## Minimum age

| Country | Minimum age |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 18 |
| UAE | 18 |
| Egypt | 16 |

## Identity documents

To verify your account you'll need a valid Saudi national ID or Iqama in Saudi Arabia, a valid Emirates ID in the UAE, or a valid Egyptian national ID card in Egypt. Photocopies, photos of a screen and expired documents are not accepted.

## Who can't open an account

- Companies, shops, charities and other organizations. See Business accounts vs personal accounts.
- Anyone who already has a Sahla Pay account. It's one account per person.
- Visitors on tourist or visit visas.

Accounts opened for someone else, or opened with another person's ID, are closed when we find them, and any balance is held until the real owner is identified.

Customers in Egypt aged 16 or over but under 21 can open an account, but a parent or legal guardian has to approve it in the app before money can be sent out. Until they approve, you can top up and receive money, but outgoing transfers and card payments stay blocked. More in Accounts for minors and guardian consent.

title: Documents required for verification in Saudi Arabia
headings: Do I need proof of address?
My Iqama is about to expire
text:
Documents required for verification in Saudi Arabia
Section: Account > Verification > Documents
Countries: Saudi Arabia

To verify an account registered in Saudi Arabia, you need a valid Saudi national ID or Iqama, and a selfie taken in the app.

## Which ID should I use?

Saudi citizens use their national ID. Residents use their Iqama. The ID must be valid on the day you submit it, and the photo, name and ID number must be easy to read.

## Can I use my passport?

No. A passport alone can't be used to verify an account registered in Saudi Arabia, even if it's valid. If you're a resident, use your Iqama.

## Is there a faster way?

Yes. If you have a Nafath account, you can verify through Nafath instead of scanning your card, and it's usually approved within minutes. See Verifying with Nafath.

## Do I need proof of address?

Not in Saudi Arabia. We use the address registered with your national ID or Iqama.

## My Iqama is about to expire

You can still verify with it, but you'll need to update it once it's renewed. Accounts with an expired Iqama are restricted after 30 calendar days. See Updating an expired ID or Iqama.

title: Documents required for verification in Egypt
headings: What counts as proof of address?
text:
Documents required for verification in Egypt
Section: Account > Verification > Documents
Countries: Egypt

To verify an account registered in Egypt, you need a valid Egyptian national ID card, a selfie, and a recent proof of address.

## Which ID is accepted?

Your Egyptian national ID card, front and back. It must be valid and not damaged. Foreign residents in Egypt can't open a Sahla Pay account at the moment.

## What counts as proof of address?

Any of these, in your name and dated within the last 3 months:

- an electricity, water or gas bill
- a landline or internet bill
- a bank statement

If the bill is in a family member's name, upload it together with a document showing you live at the same address, such as the address on the back of your national ID. More in Proof of address: when it's needed.

## I'm under 21

You can still verify with your own national ID, but a parent or guardian will need to approve your account. See Accounts for minors and guardian consent.

## How long will it take?

Manual reviews in Egypt take up to 3 business days. See How long does verification take?.

title: How to verify your identity in the app
text:
How to verify your identity in the app
Section: Account > Verification
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Verifying your identity lifts your limits and unlocks cards and international transfers. You only need to do it once, unless your ID expires.

## Before you start

- Have your original ID with you, not a copy. The documents for your country are listed in Saudi Arabia, UAE and Egypt.
- Find a well-lit spot and remove glasses and hats for the selfie.

## Verify

To verify your account:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Verify identity**.
2. Choose your document type.
3. Place your ID on a dark, flat surface and scan the front, then the back when asked.
4. Take a selfie, turning your head slowly when the app tells you to.
5. In Egypt, upload your proof of address.
6. Check your details and tap **Submit**.

## What happens next

Most checks are approved within minutes. If yours needs a manual review, you'll see **In review** on your profile; see How long does verification take?. If something isn't clear, we'll tell you exactly what to redo. If the selfie fails, see Selfie check failed.

title: How long does verification take?
headings: How long does a manual review take?
Which days count as business days?
Can I use the app while I wait?
text:
How long does verification take?
Section: Account > Verification
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Most identity checks are approved automatically a few minutes after you submit your documents. Some need a manual review by our team.

## How long does a manual review take?

It depends on the country your account is registered in:

- Saudi Arabia: up to 1 business day
- UAE: up to 2 business days
- Egypt: up to 3 business days

## Which days count as business days?

Business days are Sunday to Thursday in Saudi Arabia, Monday to Friday in the UAE, and Sunday to Thursday in Egypt. Public holidays don't count. A review submitted on a Thursday evening in Riyadh will usually be picked up on Sunday.

## Can I use the app while I wait?

Yes. Until you're verified, your account works with the limits for unverified accounts. You can top up and receive money, but sending is capped. See Unverified vs verified accounts.

## It's taking longer than this

Please don't submit your documents again. A new submission goes to the back of the queue and restarts the review. If the time above has passed, check your email and app notifications first, because we may have asked for a clearer photo. If there's nothing there, contact us through **Help** > **Chat with us**.

title: Why was my ID rejected?
text:
Why was my ID rejected?
Section: Account > Verification > Troubleshooting
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If we couldn't accept your ID, the app shows the reason under **Profile** > **Verify identity**. These are the most common ones.

## "Image unclear"

Glare, blur or a cut-off corner. Scan again on a dark surface, away from direct light, with the whole card inside the frame. Don't use the flash.

## "Document not accepted"

You uploaded a document we can't use for your country, for example a driving licence or a passport for an account in Saudi Arabia. Check the list for your country and use one of those.

## "Document expired"

The ID must be valid on the day you submit it. Renew it first, then verify.

## "Details don't match"

The name or date of birth in your profile is different from your ID. You can correct small spelling differences yourself before submitting. A different name entirely means the account was opened with someone else's details, and that can't be fixed by editing.

## Rejected more than once

You can try again straight away after most rejections. If your ID was rejected because it appears to be damaged or altered, the retry button is disabled. You'll need to contact support and may be asked to show the original card on a video call before you can try again.

title: Verification stuck "In review"
headings: Things that slow a review down
text:
Verification stuck "In review"
Section: Account > Verification > Troubleshooting
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If your profile has said **In review** for a while, your documents are waiting for a person on our verification team. That's normal for some IDs, for example older cards, worn photos, or a name that's written differently on your ID and in the app.

## How long is too long?

A manual review in Saudi Arabia finishes within 1 business day. In the UAE it's 2 business days, and in Egypt 3 business days. Weekends and public holidays aren't counted.

## Things that slow a review down

- The selfie doesn't clearly match the ID photo (glasses, a hat, poor light).
- The ID expires in the next few days.
- The name in your profile doesn't match your ID. Arabic and English spellings are compared, so small differences are fine, but a different family name is not.
- You submitted more than once. Each new submission cancels the previous one.

## What you can do

Keep the app updated and notifications on, because if we need anything else we'll ask there. If the review time for your country has passed, chat with us from **Help** in the app and we'll check where it is. We can't speed up a review that is still within the normal time.

title: Unverified vs verified accounts
text:
Unverified vs verified accounts
Section: Account > Verification
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Every Sahla Pay account starts unverified. Verifying your ID raises your limits and unlocks more of the app.

## What you can do

| | Unverified | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| Receive money and top up | Yes | Yes |
| Send to other Sahla Pay users | Yes, within lower limits | Yes |
| Send to bank accounts | No | Yes |
| International transfers | No | Yes, except in Egypt |
| Virtual and physical cards | No | Yes |

## Limits by country

| | Saudi Arabia | UAE | Egypt |
|---|---|---|---|
| Maximum balance, unverified | SAR 5,000 | AED 3,000 | EGP 20,000 |
| Maximum balance, verified | SAR 100,000 | AED 75,000 | EGP 300,000 |
| Daily sending, unverified | SAR 1,000 | AED 1,000 | EGP 5,000 |
| Daily sending, verified | SAR 20,000 | AED 15,000 | EGP 60,000 |

If someone sends you money that would take an unverified account above its maximum balance, the transfer is declined and the sender gets their money back.

More detail on sending limits is in Daily and monthly transfer limits. To verify, see How to verify your identity in the app.

title: Updating an expired ID or Iqama
headings: What happens when my ID expires?
text:
Updating an expired ID or Iqama
Section: Account > Verification > Updating your ID
Countries: Saudi Arabia

When your national ID or Iqama is renewed, update it in the app so your account stays fully active.

## What happens when my ID expires?

We'll remind you in the app before the expiry date. After it expires, your account keeps working normally for 30 calendar days. If you haven't updated it by then, outgoing transfers and card payments are paused until you do. You can still receive money and log in.

## Update your ID

To update it:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Personal details** > **ID document**.
2. Tap **Update ID**.
3. Scan the front and back of the renewed card, or confirm through Nafath.
4. Tap **Submit**.

Updates are usually approved within minutes, and the pause is lifted straight away.

## My Iqama number changed

If your Iqama number has changed, for example after a change of status, the app can't match it to your account. Don't open a new account. Contact us from **Help** > **Chat with us** and we'll update it manually after checking both documents.

title: Changing your registered phone number
headings: If you still have your old number
If you've lost access to your old number
text:
Changing your registered phone number
Section: Account > Personal details
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Your phone number is your login and where we send security codes, so changing it takes a few extra checks.

## If you still have your old number

To change it:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Personal details** > **Phone number**.
2. Enter the code we send to your current number.
3. Enter your new number, and the code we send to it.
4. Take a quick selfie to confirm it's you.

## If you've lost access to your old number

Tap **Forgot password** > **I no longer have this number** on the login screen. You'll need to scan your ID and take a selfie. The change is reviewed by our team before it takes effect.

## After the change

For your protection, sending money to new recipients and sending money abroad are blocked for 24 hours after the number changes. Transfers to recipients you've paid before and card payments work normally.

The new number must be from the same country your account is registered in. A number from another country can't be added, even temporarily. See Moving to another country.

title: Selfie check failed
headings: "We couldn't match your face to your ID"
text:
Selfie check failed
Section: Account > Verification > Troubleshooting
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

The selfie check compares your face with the photo on your ID and checks that it's a live person, not a photo of a photo.

## "We couldn't match your face to your ID"

- Take off glasses, hats and face coverings. A headscarf is fine if your face is fully visible, from forehead to chin.
- Face a window or a light, not away from it.
- Hold the phone at eye level, about an arm's length away.
- If your ID photo is very old, the match can fail even if you do everything right. Try once more, and if it fails again, contact us.

## "Please follow the instructions"

The app asks you to turn your head or blink to show you're really there. Move slowly and keep your face inside the oval until the circle completes.

## The camera won't open

See Camera not working during verification.

## Out of attempts

You can try the selfie 3 times a day. After that, the button is greyed out until the next day.

If you're still blocked the next day, or your account shows **Manual check needed**, our team will compare the photos by hand. That takes the normal manual review time for your country, and you don't need to submit anything again.

title: Accounts for minors and guardian consent
headings: Limits for accounts with a guardian
text:
Accounts for minors and guardian consent
Section: Account > Eligibility
Countries: Egypt

In Egypt, you can open a Sahla Pay account from age 16. If you're under 21, a parent or legal guardian has to approve your account before you can send money or use a card.

## How guardian approval works

1. Open your account and verify it with your own national ID.
2. In **Profile** > **Guardian**, enter your guardian's phone number.
3. Your guardian gets a request in their own Sahla Pay app and approves it.

Your guardian must have a verified Sahla Pay account registered in Egypt.

## Limits for accounts with a guardian

You can send up to EGP 2,000 a day. Your guardian can set a lower limit, see your transactions, and freeze your card from their app. They can't send money out of your account.

## When you turn 21

Your account becomes a normal account automatically on your birthday, with the standard limits for verified accounts in Egypt. Your guardian loses access, and you don't need to do anything.

International transfers stay unavailable for all accounts in Egypt, whatever your age. If your guardian closes their own Sahla Pay account, your account goes back to receive-only until you add a new guardian.

Yes. Employers can send salaries to your account from their bank like any other bank transfer.

Can I have one account for personal use and one for savings?
Can I open an account for my child or my parents?
text:
Can I have more than one account?
Section: Account > Eligibility
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

No. Each person can have one Sahla Pay account, linked to one ID.

## What if I opened a second account by mistake?

If you open a new account with the same ID, verification of the second account will fail. Use your original account instead. If you can't log in to it, use **Forgot password** on the login screen rather than signing up again.

If both accounts have money in them, contact us. We'll close the newer one and move its balance to your original account.

## Can I have one account for personal use and one for savings?

Not as separate accounts. You can use **Pockets** to set money aside inside your account. Money in a pocket isn't spent by card payments and transfers until you move it back.

## Can I open an account for my child or my parents?

Not in your name. Each person must open their own account, with their own ID and phone number. In Egypt, a parent can approve an account opened by a child aged 16 or over; see Accounts for minors and guardian consent.

title: Why we ask you to verify again
headings: What do I need to do?
What if I don't do it?
text:
Why we ask you to verify again
Section: Account > Verification
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Sometimes we ask customers who are already verified to confirm their details again. This is a legal requirement for payment companies, not a sign that something is wrong with your account.

## When does this happen?

- Every 2 years, as a routine check.
- When your ID expires.
- If your activity changes a lot, for example you start receiving much larger amounts.
- If we detect a login from a new device together with other unusual activity.

## What do I need to do?

Open the notification or go to **Profile** > **Verify identity**. Usually it's just a new selfie. Sometimes we also ask for your ID again, or a few questions about how you use the account.

## What if I don't do it?

We'll remind you several times. If you still haven't completed it by the date in the notification, sending money and card payments are paused until you do. Receiving money keeps working.

If we've asked about the source of your money, see Source of funds questions.

Section: Account > Verification
Countries: Saudi Arabia

- Install the Nafath app and make sure you can log in to it.

1. Go to **Profile** > **Verify identity** > **Verify with Nafath**.

title: Source of funds questions
headings: What happens to my account in the meantime?
text:
Source of funds questions
Section: Account > Verification
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Like all regulated payment companies, we have to understand where large amounts of money come from. If your account receives a lot more than usual, we'll ask you a few questions.

## When do you ask?

Usually when the money you receive in one calendar month goes above SAR 50,000 in Saudi Arabia, AED 50,000 in the UAE or EGP 250,000 in Egypt. We may also ask below these amounts if the activity looks unusual for your account.

## What will you ask for?

A short form in the app: what you do for work, where the money came from, and who sends it. Sometimes we ask for a document, such as:

- a salary certificate or recent payslip
- a sale contract, for example for a car
- a bank statement showing the money before it came to Sahla Pay

## What happens to my account in the meantime?

Your account keeps working while you answer. Once you've submitted everything, our team reviews it within a few business days.

If you don't reply by the date in our message, outgoing transfers are paused until you do. Money that arrives during a review isn't returned to the sender automatically. It stays in your balance, but you can't send it on until the review is closed.

title: Linking a bank account
headings: Why was my bank account rejected?
text:
Linking a bank account
Section: Account > Bank accounts
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Linking your own bank account makes it quicker to top up and to move money back to your bank. You can link up to 3 bank accounts.

## Before you start

- Your Sahla Pay account must be verified.
- The bank account must be in your own name and in the same country as your Sahla Pay account.
- Have your IBAN ready. You'll find it in your banking app or on your bank statement.

## Link your bank account

To link an account:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Bank accounts** > **Add bank account**.
2. Enter your IBAN. The bank name is filled in automatically.
3. Confirm that the account is in your name.
4. Enter the code we send to your phone.

## What happens next

We check the name on the bank account with your bank. This usually takes a few minutes, but can take up to one business day. You'll see **Linked** next to the account when it's ready.

Moving money to a linked bank account in your own name doesn't count towards your monthly transfer limit. See Daily and monthly transfer limits.

## Why was my bank account rejected?

The most common reason is that the name on the bank account doesn't match your Sahla Pay name, for example a joint account or a company account. Only personal accounts in your own name can be linked.

## Remove a bank account

To remove it:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Bank accounts**.
2. Tap the account you want to remove.
3. Tap **Remove** and confirm with the code we send you.

Removing a bank account here doesn't affect the bank account itself, only its link to Sahla Pay.

## What about scheduled transfers?

Any scheduled or recurring transfers to that bank account are cancelled when you remove it. You'll see them disappear from **Payments** > **Scheduled**.

If a transfer to the account is already **Processing** when you remove it, it still goes through. It can't be stopped by removing the account.

You can't remove a bank account that you've chosen to receive your balance after closing your Sahla Pay account, while that closure is in progress.

Everything in your account, including money in Pockets. Pending refunds count once they arrive.

title: Getting started: your first top-up
headings: Top up with a debit card
text:
Getting started: your first top-up
Section: Account > Getting started
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

To start paying and sending money, add money to your Sahla Pay balance. You can top up with a debit card or by bank transfer.

## Minimum top-up

| Country | Minimum per top-up |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | SAR 10 |
| UAE | AED 10 |
| Egypt | EGP 50 |

## Top up with a debit card

To top up by card:

1. On the home screen, tap **Add money** > **Debit card**.
2. Enter the amount.
3. Add your card details, or choose a saved card.
4. Confirm the payment in your bank's app or with the code your bank sends you.

The money arrives in your balance straight away. A small fee applies to card top-ups; see Top-up fees.

## Top up by bank transfer

Bank transfers are free. Tap **Add money** > **Bank transfer** to see your Sahla Pay IBAN, then send money to it from your banking app. See Topping up by bank transfer.

Credit cards can't be used for top-ups, and neither can prepaid cards issued by other companies. The payment will be declined by us even if your bank approves it.

title: Verification FAQ
headings: Why do I have to verify?
Can I verify with someone else's ID?
Is my ID safe with you?
I'm verified but the app still asks me to verify
text:
Verification FAQ
Section: Account > Verification
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Quick answers to the questions we get most about verifying your account.

## Why do I have to verify?

It's a legal requirement for payment accounts, and it protects you: it's much harder for someone to open an account in your name.

## Is verification free?

Yes, always.

## How long does it take?

Usually a few minutes. Manual reviews take up to 1 business day in Saudi Arabia, 2 business days in the UAE and 3 business days in Egypt.

## What changes after I verify?

You can send more, hold more and get a card. For example, in Saudi Arabia your daily sending limit goes from SAR 1,000 to SAR 20,000. In the UAE it goes from AED 1,000 to AED 15,000, and in Egypt from EGP 5,000 to EGP 60,000.

## Can I verify with someone else's ID?

No. The ID has to belong to you, and the selfie has to match it. Accounts verified with another person's ID are closed.

## Is my ID safe with you?

Your documents are encrypted and only used for verification and legal checks. We never share them with merchants or other users.

## I'm verified but the app still asks me to verify

You may have been asked to re-verify. See Why we ask you to verify again.

title: Sending money to another Sahla Pay user
headings: What if they don't have Sahla Pay yet?
Can I send to a Sahla Pay user in another country?
text:
Sending money to another Sahla Pay user
Section: Transfers > Sending money
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Sending money to someone with a Sahla Pay account in the same country is free and arrives instantly, any day of the week.

## Send money

To send:

1. Tap **Send** > **To a Sahla Pay user**.
2. Pick a contact, or enter their phone number.
3. Check the name that appears. It's the name on their verified account.
4. Enter the amount and, if you like, a note.
5. Tap **Send** and confirm with your fingerprint, face or passcode.

## What if they don't have Sahla Pay yet?

You can still send to their phone number. They'll get an SMS inviting them to join. If they don't open an account and claim it, the money comes back to you; see Unclaimed transfers.

## Can I send to a Sahla Pay user in another country?

No. Transfers between users only work within the same country. To send to someone abroad, use an international transfer to their bank account; see Sending money abroad.

## Limits

Transfers to other users count towards your daily and monthly limits. See Daily and monthly transfer limits.

title: Sending money to a local bank account
text:
Sending money to a local bank account
Section: Transfers > Sending money
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can send money from your balance to any bank account in the country your Sahla Pay account is registered in.

## Before you start

- Your account must be verified.
- You'll need the recipient's IBAN and their full name as their bank has it.

## Send to a bank account

To send:

1. Tap **Send** > **To a bank account**.
2. Enter the IBAN, or choose a saved recipient.
3. Enter the recipient's name and the amount.
4. Check the fee and tap **Confirm**.
5. Enter the code we send to your phone if it's a new recipient.

## When will it arrive?

| Country | Usual arrival time |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | within a few minutes (including weekends) |
| UAE | 1 business day |
| Egypt | within a few minutes (including weekends) |

The fee depends on your country; see Local transfer fees.

## The name doesn't match

In Saudi Arabia and Egypt, the recipient's bank checks the name before accepting the transfer. If the name you entered is very different, the transfer is returned to your balance within a few minutes, with no fee charged. In the UAE the check happens later, so a returned transfer can take up to 3 business days to come back.

title: Daily and monthly transfer limits
text:
Daily and monthly transfer limits
Section: Transfers > Limits
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

These limits apply to money you send from your Sahla Pay balance: to other Sahla Pay users, to bank accounts, and abroad. They depend on whether your account is verified and on the country your account is registered in.

| Limit | Saudi Arabia | UAE | Egypt |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daily, verified account | SAR 20,000 | AED 15,000 | EGP 60,000 |
| Monthly, verified account | SAR 100,000 | AED 75,000 | EGP 200,000 |
| Daily, unverified account | SAR 1,000 | AED 1,000 | EGP 5,000 |

Unverified accounts don't have a separate monthly limit, but the balance cap still applies. See Wallet balance limits.

Card payments, bill payments and QR payments in shops don't count towards these limits. They have their own limits, listed in the articles for each service.

Daily limits reset at midnight in your account's country, and monthly limits on the 1st of each month. If a transfer fails or is cancelled, the amount is added back to your available limit straight away. A transfer you've disputed only comes back once the dispute is closed.

Money you move to a bank account in your own name counts towards the daily limit but not the monthly one. The app checks the name on the receiving account, so this only works for accounts you've linked under **Profile** > **Bank accounts**. See Linking a bank account.

Need more? See Can I increase my limits?.

text:

Section: Transfers > International
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can send money from your Sahla Pay balance to a bank account in another country. The recipient gets the money in their local currency.

4. Add the recipient's bank details, or pick a saved recipient.
5. Check the exchange rate, the fee and the amount the recipient will receive.

## What happens next

You'll see the transfer under **Activity** as **Processing**. Most transfers arrive the same day; see How long do international transfers take? for the maximum times. You'll get a notification when the receiving bank accepts it.

title: International transfer fees
text:
International transfer fees
Section: Transfers > International > Fees
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE

This is what you pay when you send money to a bank account abroad from an account registered in Saudi Arabia or the UAE.

| | Saudi Arabia | UAE |
|---|---|---|
| Transfer fee | 1.5% of the amount sent | 1.25% of the amount sent |
| Minimum fee per transfer | SAR 15 | AED 15 |
| Exchange rate markup | 2.5% | 2% |

The fee is calculated on the amount you send, in your own currency, and is taken from your balance on top of that amount. The app shows the fee and the exact amount the recipient will get before you confirm.

The exchange rate markup is not a separate charge. It's included in the rate we show you, which is the reference rate plus the markup.

VAT is added to the transfer fee: 15% in Saudi Arabia and 5% in the UAE. It isn't added to the exchange rate markup.

The minimum fee applies to every transfer, so splitting one large transfer into several small ones usually costs more in total. The recipient's bank or an intermediary bank may also take its own fee. We don't control or receive those fees, and they can reduce the amount that arrives.

title: How long do international transfers take?
headings: Why is my transfer taking longer?
text:
How long do international transfers take?
Section: Transfers > International
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE

Most international transfers arrive the same day. The maximum time depends on where you're sending from.

## Maximum delivery times

- From Saudi Arabia: 2 business days
- From the UAE: 1 business day

The time is counted from when your transfer shows **Sent to bank** in the app, in our business days. Business days are Sunday to Thursday in Saudi Arabia and Monday to Friday in the UAE.

## Why is my transfer taking longer?

- **It's a weekend or holiday in the recipient's country.** Their bank may only credit the money on its next working day.
- **The receiving bank is checking it.** Some banks hold large or first-time transfers for their own checks.
- **The details need fixing.** We'll message you if the bank asks for more information.

## Transfers held for review

Before a transfer leaves Sahla Pay, it may be held for a security review, especially the first time you send to a new recipient or when the amount is large. The review usually takes a few hours. The delivery time above only starts once it's finished, and the status shows **Under review** until then.

title: Receiving money from abroad
headings: What details do I give the sender?
text:
Receiving money from abroad
Section: Transfers > International
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can receive international transfers into your Sahla Pay balance in all three countries, including Egypt.

## What details do I give the sender?

Go to **Add money** > **Bank transfer** > **From abroad**. You'll see your name, your Sahla Pay IBAN and our bank's SWIFT code. Send these to the person paying you.

## Is there a fee?

Receiving is free on our side. The sender's bank, and sometimes an intermediary bank, may take a fee, so you can receive a little less than was sent.

## How long does it take?

Up to 3 business days after the sender's bank releases the money. Money sent in another currency is converted to your local currency when it arrives, at our rate on that day.

## The money hasn't arrived

Ask the sender for the transfer receipt, sometimes called an MT103, and share it with us through **Help** > **Chat with us**.

Incoming transfers count towards your balance limit. If the amount would take you over it, the transfer is returned to the sender, and their bank may charge them for the return. Unverified accounts can't receive international transfers at all.

title: Why did my transfer fail?
text:
Why did my transfer fail?
Section: Transfers > Problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

When a transfer fails, the app shows a reason on the transfer in **Activity**. Here's what each one means.

## "Limit reached"

You've reached your daily or monthly limit. Try again after it resets, or see Daily and monthly transfer limits.

## "Insufficient balance"

Your balance doesn't cover the amount plus the fee. Top up and try again.

## "Recipient can't receive this amount"

The recipient's account would go over its balance limit, usually because it isn't verified. Ask them to verify, or send a smaller amount.

## "Rejected by the recipient's bank"

The IBAN or name is wrong, or the bank account is closed. Check the details with the recipient.

## "Blocked for your security"

Our systems stopped the transfer because it looked unusual. Nothing has been sent. Check your notifications, because we may ask you to confirm it was you.

## Was the money taken?

A failed transfer shouldn't take money from your balance. If it did, see A failed payment was deducted from my balance.

title: A failed payment was deducted from my balance
text:
A failed payment was deducted from my balance
Section: Transfers > Problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Sometimes a payment or transfer fails, but the amount still disappears from your balance. The money isn't lost. It's held while the systems on both sides confirm the payment didn't go through.

## How long until it's back?

| Country | Reversed within |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 2 business days |
| UAE | 3 business days |
| Egypt | 5 business days |

It comes back automatically, and you'll get a notification. You don't need to report it.

## It's been longer than that

Section: Transfers > Sending money

## Transfers to someone who hasn't joined yet

text:

Section: Transfers > Sending money
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## Set up a scheduled transfer

To schedule a transfer:

1. Start a transfer as usual, to a Sahla Pay user or a bank account.
2. Before confirming, tap **Send later**.
3. Pick a date, up to 12 months ahead, and choose **Once**, **Weekly** or **Monthly**.
4. Tap **Schedule**.

Scheduled transfers are sent at 8:00 AM local time on the chosen day. You'll find them under **Payments** > **Scheduled**.

## What if I don't have enough money?

## Monthly transfers at the end of the month

If you choose the 29th, 30th or 31st, the transfer is sent on the last day of shorter months.

International transfers can't be scheduled. Scheduled transfers also count towards your limits on the day they're sent, not the day you set them up.

title: Transfer statuses explained
headings: How long can a transfer stay "Pending"?
Does "Completed" mean the recipient can see it?
text:
Transfer statuses explained
Section: Transfers > Tracking
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Every transfer in **Activity** has a status. Here's what each one means.

| Status | What it means |
|---|---|
| Pending | We've received your transfer and are processing it. It can still be cancelled. |
| Under review | Held for a security check before it's sent. |
| Waiting for recipient | Sent to a phone number that isn't on Sahla Pay yet. |
| Processing | Sent to the recipient's bank, which hasn't confirmed yet. |
| Sent to bank | An international transfer has left Sahla Pay. |
| Completed | The money has arrived. |
| Failed | Nothing was sent. The reason is shown on the transfer. |
| Returned | The recipient's bank sent the money back. |
| Cancelled | You cancelled it, or it expired before it was claimed. |

## How long can a transfer stay "Pending"?

Usually a few seconds. If it's still pending after an hour, contact us.

## Does "Completed" mean the recipient can see it?

For transfers to Sahla Pay users, yes. For bank transfers, it means the receiving bank has accepted it. Most banks show it in the recipient's account straight away, but some take longer.

title: Currency conversion and exchange rates
headings: Should I pay in my own currency abroad?
text:
Currency conversion and exchange rates
Section: Payments > Foreign currency
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

When money changes currency, through an international transfer or a card payment in another currency, we convert it at our exchange rate.

## How our rate works

Our rate is a reference market rate plus a markup:

| Country | Markup |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 2.5% |
| UAE | 2% |
| Egypt | 3% |

The markup is included in the rate you see, not charged separately.

## When is the rate set?

For international transfers, when you confirm. The rate is locked, and the recipient gets exactly the amount shown.

For card payments, when the payment is completed by the card network, which can be a day or two after you paid. The amount can differ slightly from what you saw at the till.

## Should I pay in my own currency abroad?

When a shop or ATM abroad offers to charge you in your home currency, choose the local currency instead. The shop's conversion is usually more expensive than ours.

Refunds in a foreign currency are converted back at the rate on the day of the refund, so you may get back a little more or less than you paid. See Refunds in a different currency.

## A shop or website said they've refunded me

Once the merchant has sent the refund, it reaches your Sahla Pay balance within 7 business days in Saudi Arabia, 10 business days in the UAE and 14 business days in Egypt. Before that, the merchant has to process it on their side, and we can't see or speed that part up.

## I paid but the payment failed

Sometimes a payment fails but the money still leaves your balance. It comes back automatically: within 2 business days in Saudi Arabia, 3 business days in the UAE and 5 business days in Egypt. You don't need to contact us unless that time has passed.

## I sent money to the wrong person and opened a dispute

If we approve your dispute, the money is returned within 5 business days (Saudi Arabia), 7 business days (UAE) or 10 business days (Egypt). That time starts when the dispute is approved, not when you open it.

## Business days?

Yes, all of these are business days, and public holidays don't count.

If we approve your dispute, the money is returned within 5 business days (Saudi Arabia), 7 business days (UAE) or 10 business days (Egypt). That time starts when the dispute is approved, not when you open it.

Yes, all of these are business days, and public holidays don't count.

title: Chargebacks explained
text:
Chargebacks explained
Section: Refunds and disputes > Disputes
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

A chargeback is how we get your money back from a merchant's bank when a card dispute can't be solved directly. It runs under the rules of the card network, not just our own.

## How it works

1. We review your dispute and decide whether it qualifies for a chargeback.
2. We send the chargeback to the merchant's bank, with your evidence.
3. The merchant can accept it, or respond with their own evidence.
4. If they respond, we review both sides, and may send the case back to them once more.

The whole process can take up to 90 calendar days, mainly because the merchant has time to respond at each step.

## What can't be charged back?

- Transfers to other Sahla Pay users or bank accounts. These are handled as transfer disputes instead.
- QR payments, which don't use the card network.
- Payments you approved and later regretted, if the merchant delivered what was described.

## What if the merchant wins?

You'll get the merchant's evidence and the reasons for our decision. Any temporary credit we gave you is taken back.

Chargebacks are also not available when the merchant is a gambling or crypto service, even if the card payment was approved. Disputes about these payments are reviewed only as possible fraud.

text:

Section: Refunds and disputes > Card problems
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Seeing the same payment twice? Before disputing it, check whether one of them is just a hold.

## One says "Pending", the other "Completed"

This is usually a hold plus the final charge. Hotels, petrol stations and car rental companies often place a hold first and then charge the final amount separately. The hold drops off on its own within 7 calendar days. See Merchant holds and pre-authorizations.

## Both say "Completed"

You may really have been charged twice. Contact the merchant first and ask them to refund one of the payments. If they don't, open a dispute from either payment: **Report a problem** > **I was charged twice**.

## The amounts are slightly different

This often happens with payments in a foreign currency, or tips added after the payment. It's usually two different charges, not a duplicate.

If you paid twice yourself, for example because the first payment seemed to fail and you tried again, it's not a duplicate charge for dispute purposes. Ask the merchant for a refund of the extra payment.

Sometimes a merchant refunds only part of a payment, for example when you return one item from an order.

As a separate refund line in **Activity**, for the amount the merchant refunded. The original payment stays as it was.

- Only some of the items were returned.

title: Transactions I didn't make
headings: Will I get my money back?
text:
Transactions I didn't make
Section: Refunds and disputes > Fraud
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If you see a payment or transfer you didn't make or approve, act straight away.

## Do this now

To protect your account:

1. Freeze your card: **Cards** > **Freeze**.
2. Change your password: **Profile** > **Security** > **Change password**.
3. Report the transaction: tap it in **Activity** > **Report a problem** > **I didn't make this**.

## Will I get my money back?

If you report an unauthorized transaction within 2 calendar days of noticing it, and you didn't share your password, PIN or one-time passwords with anyone, we refund it in full once we've confirmed it was unauthorized.

If you report it later, the most you'll lose is SAR 500 in Saudi Arabia, AED 500 in the UAE or EGP 2,000 in Egypt, unless you acted fraudulently or with gross negligence.

title: Refunds in a different currency
headings: Why didn't I get back exactly what I paid?
Can you refund me the difference?
The merchant refunded in my own currency
text:
Refunds in a different currency
Section: Refunds and disputes > Refunds
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If you paid in a foreign currency, the merchant refunds you in that same currency, and we convert it back.

## Why didn't I get back exactly what I paid?

Because the refund is converted on the day it arrives, not the day you paid. If the exchange rate moved in between, you may get a little more or a little less.

The markup in our rate also applies again when the refund is converted: 2.5% in Saudi Arabia, 2% in the UAE and 3% in Egypt. So even if the rate didn't move at all, a foreign-currency refund comes back slightly lower than the original payment.

## Can you refund me the difference?

No. Exchange rate differences on refunds aren't something we can refund, because we don't control the rate or when the merchant sends the refund.

## The merchant refunded in my own currency

Then no conversion is needed, and you get exactly the amount they sent.

title: Merchant refund policies vs Sahla Pay policies
text:
Merchant refund policies vs Sahla Pay policies
Section: Refunds and disputes > Refunds
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Two different sets of rules can apply when you want your money back, and it helps to know which one you're dealing with.

## The merchant's policy

Each shop decides whether it accepts returns, for how long, and whether it refunds money, gives store credit, or exchanges items. This is between you and the merchant. Sahla Pay can't make a merchant accept a return that their policy doesn't allow.

## Sahla Pay's policies

Our rules cover:

- how quickly a refund reaches your balance once the merchant sends it (Refund timelines)
- disputes, when a merchant didn't deliver, charged you wrongly, or broke their own policy (Disputing a card transaction)
- payments you didn't make (Transactions I didn't make)

## An example

You bought shoes, changed your mind, and the shop's policy says "no refunds on sale items". That's the merchant's decision, and a dispute won't change it. But if the shop promised a refund in writing and never sent it, that's something we can help with.

title: Cancelling a dispute
headings: What happens to a temporary credit?
text:
Cancelling a dispute
Section: Refunds and disputes > Disputes
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

If the merchant refunded you, or you recognize the payment after all, you can cancel your dispute.

## Cancel a dispute

To cancel:

1. Go to **Help** > **My cases** and open the case.
2. Tap **Cancel dispute**.
3. Tell us why, for example "Merchant refunded me".

The case is closed straight away.

## What happens to a temporary credit?

If we gave you a temporary credit for the dispute, it's taken back from your balance when you cancel. If the merchant has refunded you as well, you'd otherwise get the money twice.

## Can I reopen it?

No. Once cancelled, a dispute can't be reopened, and you can't open a new one for the same payment.

Disputes that have already been sent to the merchant's bank as a chargeback can't be cancelled from the app. Message us from the case instead, and we'll withdraw it if the card network rules allow.

title: Disputes for international transfers
headings: Sent to the wrong person, or want it back
text:
Disputes for international transfers
Section: Refunds and disputes > Disputes
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE

International transfers go through other banks, sometimes several, so getting money back after it's sent is harder than for local transfers.

## Wrong details

If the IBAN or name was wrong, the receiving bank usually returns the transfer on its own. The amount comes back to your balance in your currency, at the exchange rate on the day it returns.

## Sent to the wrong person, or want it back

We can ask the receiving bank to return the money. This is called a recall. Open the transfer in **Activity** and tap **Report a problem** > **Recall this transfer**.

A recall costs SAR 50 in Saudi Arabia and AED 50 in the UAE. The receiving bank decides whether to return the money, and it usually needs the recipient's agreement. Recalls can take several weeks.

## Scams

If you were tricked into sending the transfer, report it as fraud straight away. The sooner we contact the receiving bank, the better the chance of stopping the money.

The recall fee is charged even if the receiving bank refuses to return the money, and it isn't refunded. If the bank does return it, intermediary banks may deduct their own fees, so you may get back less than you sent.

title: Fraudulent merchants
headings: I paid a fake shop by card
text:
Fraudulent merchants
Section: Refunds and disputes > Fraud
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Some online shops exist only to take payments and never deliver. If you think you've paid one, here's how we handle it.

## Signs of a fake shop

- Prices far below everywhere else, especially for phones, perfume and electronics.
- Only social media pages, no proper website or contact details.
- Asks you to pay by transfer to a personal account instead of by card.
- The shop disappears or blocks you after you pay.

## I paid a fake shop by card

Open a dispute from the payment as **Goods not received**. Card payments are protected by the card network rules, so you have a good chance of getting your money back. See Goods or services not received.

## I paid by transfer

Transfers to a person, rather than card payments, aren't covered by chargeback rules. Report it as fraud as soon as possible; we'll try to freeze the money in the recipient's account. See Reporting fraud.

## What happens to the merchant?

When we see several reports about the same merchant, we block card payments to them for all our customers and report them to the card network.

## How long does delivery take?

| Country | Delivery within |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 5 business days |
| UAE | 3 business days |
| Egypt | 10 business days |

## Can I track my card?

Yes. Go to **Cards** > **Track delivery**. Once the courier has it, you'll also get an SMS from them with a tracking link, and they'll call before delivering.

text:

Section: Cards > PIN

## What still works

Online payments and payments through Apple Pay or Google Pay keep working, because they don't use your PIN. Contactless payments below the no-PIN limit may also work.

## Unblock your PIN

To unblock it:

1. Go to **Cards** > **Card settings** > **Unblock PIN**.
2. Confirm it's you.
3. Check your PIN with **Show PIN**, or set a new one.

If the ATM kept your card after the wrong PIN attempts, the card can't be returned to you. Freeze it in the app and order a replacement; the lost-card fee doesn't apply when an ATM keeps your card.

text:

Section: Cards > Security

## Unfreeze it

## What still happens while my card is frozen?

Recurring payments and subscriptions are also declined while the card is frozen. If you keep it frozen for a long time, update the card details with those merchants, or you may miss a payment.

text:
Virtual cards
Section: Cards > Virtual cards
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

A virtual card is a card that lives in the app. It has its own number, expiry date and CVV, and spends from your balance like a physical card.

## How do I get one?

In Saudi Arabia and the UAE, every verified account gets a virtual card automatically. You'll find it under **Cards**. In Egypt, tap **Cards** > **Get a virtual card**, because the card has a one-time fee and we don't create it until you ask.

| Country | Virtual card |
|---|---|

| UAE | free |

Online, in apps, and in shops through Apple Pay, Google Pay or Samsung Pay, where available in your country. You can't use it at ATMs or for chip-and-PIN payments, because there's no physical chip.

## Can I delete a virtual card?

Yes: **Card settings** > **Close card**. Subscriptions on that card will stop working.

headings: I got an approval request for a payment I'm not making

text:
Online payments and 3-D Secure
Section: Cards > Paying online
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

When you pay online, many shops ask you to approve the payment in the Sahla Pay app. This is 3-D Secure, and it stops anyone using your card details without your phone.

## How does it work?

1. You enter your card details on the shop's website.
2. We send a notification to your phone.
3. Open it, check the shop name and amount, and tap **Approve**.

You have 5 minutes to approve. After that, the payment is cancelled and you'll need to start again.

## I didn't get the notification

Open the Sahla Pay app directly. Pending approvals appear at the top of the home screen. If notifications are off, you'll get an SMS code instead.

## I got an approval request for a payment I'm not making

Tap **Decline**, freeze your card, and report it. Someone has your card details.

## Some payments don't ask me to approve

That's normal. Some merchants, such as subscriptions you've already approved once, don't use 3-D Secure for repeat payments.

Payments approved with 3-D Secure are treated as authorized by you. If you approve a payment that turns out to be a scam, the protection for unauthorized transactions doesn't apply.

text:

Section: Cards > Getting a card
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Cards are delivered within 5 business days in Saudi Arabia, 3 business days in the UAE and 10 business days in Egypt. If yours hasn't arrived yet, check these first.

## Check the tracking

Go to **Cards** > **Track delivery**. The status shows whether the courier has your card, tried to deliver it, or returned it to us.

## The courier couldn't deliver

After two failed attempts, the card is returned to us. You'll see **Returned** in the tracking. Tap **Arrange delivery** to choose a new date or a different address.

## It's been longer than the delivery time

Wait 5 business days after the expected delivery date, in case of delays. If it still hasn't come, tap **Card not received** in the tracking screen. We'll cancel that card and send a new one.

## Is there a fee for the new card?

No. A card that never arrived is replaced free of charge.

title: Merchant holds and pre-authorizations
headings: What does a hold look like?
Can you release a hold early?
text:
Merchant holds and pre-authorizations
Section: Cards > Paying in shops
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Some merchants reserve money on your card before charging you the final amount. This is called a hold or pre-authorization.

## Where do holds happen?

Hotels, car rental, petrol stations, and some online shops and subscriptions that check your card with a small amount.

## What does a hold look like?

A **Pending** payment in **Activity**. The amount is taken from your available balance but hasn't been paid to the merchant.

## When is it released?

When the merchant charges the final amount, the hold is replaced by the real payment. If the merchant doesn't charge anything, the hold drops off on its own within 7 calendar days.

## Can you release a hold early?

We can't, because the merchant decides. Ask the merchant to cancel the pre-authorization; once they do, the money is usually back within a day.

Hotels and car rental companies are allowed to keep a hold for longer, up to 30 calendar days, for example to cover damage or extra nights. These holds are released when the merchant closes your booking, not after the standard time.

No. Each account has one physical card at a time. If you order a replacement, the old one stops working.

text:

Section: Cards > Paying online
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

Subscriptions, memberships and other regular payments can be charged to your Sahla Pay card automatically.

## Where can I see them?

Go to **Cards** > **Recurring payments**. We list every merchant that has charged your card on a repeating basis, with the last payment date and amount.

## How do I stop one?

Cancel with the merchant. That's the only way to end the agreement. To stop the merchant from charging your card anyway, tap the merchant and choose **Block**. See Subscription charges I don't recognize.

## What happens if my balance is too low?

The payment is declined. Many merchants try again a few days later, and may pause your subscription in the meantime.

## My card was replaced

Many merchants receive your new card details automatically through the card network and keep charging without interruption. Others don't. Check **Recurring payments** after a replacement.

Because some merchants update automatically, a subscription can keep charging your new card even after you replaced the card to get away from it. Blocking the merchant is the reliable way to stop it.

title: Dormant account fees
text:
Dormant account fees
Section: Fees and limits > Account fees
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

An account becomes dormant when you haven't made any transaction yourself for a while. Money you receive, interest and fees don't count; it has to be something you did, like a payment, a transfer or a top-up.

| Country | Dormant after | Monthly dormancy fee |
|---|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 12 months | no fee |
| UAE | 12 months | AED 10 per month |
| Egypt | 18 months | EGP 20 per month |

We'll email you and send an app notification before your account becomes dormant, so you have time to use it.

To make your account active again, log in and make any transaction, even a small top-up. The fee stops from the next month.

The dormancy fee is only taken from money in your balance. It never takes your balance below zero, and if your balance is zero, nothing is charged and nothing is owed. Accounts that stay dormant with a zero balance may eventually be closed; see Dormant accounts.

title: One-time passwords (OTP)
headings: How long is a code valid?
Will Sahla Pay ever ask me for my code?
Can I get codes by email instead?
text:
One-time passwords (OTP)
Section: Security > Logging in
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

A one-time password (OTP) is a 6-digit code we send by SMS to your registered phone number. We ask for it when you log in on a new device, add a recipient, send money abroad, or change your security settings.

## How long is a code valid?

Each code works once and expires after 5 minutes. If it expires, request a new one. Only the latest code works, so older codes stop working as soon as you ask for a new one.

## I didn't get the code

Wait 60 seconds and tap **Resend code**. If it still doesn't arrive, see Not receiving OTP codes.

## Will Sahla Pay ever ask me for my code?

No. Nobody from Sahla Pay will ever call, message or email you asking for an OTP, your PIN or your password. If someone asks, it's a scam, even if the caller knows your name or recent transactions. Hang up and report it from **Help** > **Report fraud**.

## Can I get codes by email instead?

Not at the moment. Codes are only sent by SMS to the phone number on your account. If you've changed your number, update it first; see Changing your registered phone number.

title: Account locked after failed login attempts
headings: My card is still working, is that normal?
text:
Account locked after failed login attempts
Section: Security > Logging in
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

## "Too many attempts. Try again later."

To protect your money, the app locks login after 5 wrong passwords in a row. The lock lasts 30 minutes. After that you can try again.

## I've forgotten my password

Don't keep guessing. Tap **Forgot password** on the login screen, confirm your phone number with the code we send, and set a new password. Resetting your password ends the lock straight away.

## My card is still working, is that normal?

Yes. A login lock only affects the app. Your card and any scheduled transfers keep working. If you think someone else has been trying to get into your account, freeze your card from the website or by calling the number on the back of your card.

## Locked again?

If your account is locked 3 times within one day, it's restricted for your protection, and the timer no longer unlocks it. Resetting your password won't lift it either. Only our support team can, after checking your identity. Contact us through **Help** on the login screen.

title: Contacting customer support
text:
Contacting customer support
Section: Help > Contact us
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

The fastest way to reach us is in the app: tap **Help** > **Chat with us**. You'll talk to a person, in Arabic or English, and your account details are already attached, so you don't need to repeat them.

## When are you available?

| Country | Chat and phone hours |
|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | 24 hours a day, 7 days a week |
| UAE | 24 hours a day, 7 days a week |
| Egypt | 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM Cairo time, every day |

Outside these hours, you can still leave a chat message and we'll reply when we open.

## Can I call you?

Yes. The number for your country is on the back of your card and under **Help** > **Call us**. If you call, we'll confirm your identity with a code sent to your phone.

## Urgent: lost card or fraud

You don't need to wait for us. Freeze your card instantly in **Cards** > **Freeze**. It works at any time, including outside support hours, and you can unfreeze it yourself if you find the card.

## Email

We don't handle account questions by email, because we can't confirm who is writing. Emails asking for personal details that appear to come from us are not from us.

title: Closing your account
text:
Closing your account
Section: Account > Closing your account
Countries: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt

You can close your Sahla Pay account at any time, for free. Deleting the app does not close your account; see Deleting the app vs closing your account.

## Before you start

- Download any statements you need. After closing, you won't have access to the app. We keep records for 24 months in the app, and you'd have to ask support for older ones.
- Cancel subscriptions and saved card payments, and tell anyone who sends you money regularly.
- Make sure there are no pending transfers.

## Close your account

To close your account:

1. Go to **Profile** > **Account settings** > **Close account**.
2. Tell us why (optional, but it helps us).
3. Choose a bank account in your name for any remaining balance.
4. Confirm with the code we send to your phone.

## What happens to my balance?

Your remaining balance is sent to the bank account you chose within 3 business days in Saudi Arabia, 5 business days in the UAE or 7 business days in Egypt. Your cards stop working immediately.

You can't close your account while a dispute is open. Wait for the dispute to finish, or cancel it, and then try again. Refunds that arrive after closing are sent to the same bank account; see Refunds after account closure.
